currentContext.strengths: Part of the SPGPrints Group (Boxmeer, Netherlands), giving access to a global network of competence centres, 09 international operating facilities and customers in over 100 countries|Designated lead entity for the Textile Business of the SPGPrints Group and a global competence centre within the SPGPrints network, particularly for rotary screen-printing solutions demanding high precision|Over five decades of engineering heritage (founded 1973) and over three decades of expertise in specialised textile technologies and printing solutions|In-house research and development facility recognised by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, Ministry of Science and Technology, supporting product innovation and process optimisation|Pioneer in printing innovations, including launching the first digital textile printer|Full-range portfolio covering both capital equipment and consumables for the textile printing industry, positioning it for hybrid rotary-digital production models|Fully air-conditioned Ahmedabad plant supporting high quality standards in perforated rotary screen production
currentContext.strategies: Technology as the cornerstone of the growth strategy - engineering excellence, product innovation and customer-centric solutions to support the evolving needs of the textile and printing industries.|Operate as the designated lead entity for the SPGPrints Group's Textile Business following the Group's strategic restructuring, moving from a centralized operating model to a business-unit-driven structure that places ownership, accountability and customer proximity at the heart of decision-making.|Run Ahmedabad as the central hub and global centre of the Textile Business Unit, owning product lifecycle management, technology development and innovation, manufacturing control and quality assurance, and strategic planning - to ensure consistency in product standards and efficient utilisation of manufacturing capabilities.|Serve both traditional rotary and modern digital textile printing requirements with a full capital-plus-consumables portfolio, positioning for hybrid rotary-digital production models.|Enhance product capabilities, improve operational efficiencies and deliver high-performance solutions that let customers achieve superior productivity and quality.|Maintain disciplined capital allocation and a focus on efficiency, aligned to a roadmap tracking industry trends.|Strengthen the workforce through skill development and upskilling in digital technologies, process optimization and customer-centric solutions.|Engage the market through participation in textile and label industry exhibitions to build long-term customer relationships.
currentContext.expansion: The routed sections disclose no company-specific expansion or capex project for Stovec - no new line, plant, capacity addition, commissioning or ramp-up timeline is stated. The only footprint statements are that the Ahmedabad site houses the registered cum corporate office and factory in the same premises and functions as the central hub and global centre of the SPGPrints Textile Business Unit, and that the Company runs an in-house R&D facility recognised by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research. The Company has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture. Expansion-related commentary in the bundle is about the INDUSTRY (PM MITRA parks, the PLI scheme, National Technical Textiles Mission, growing global textile manufacturing capacity), not about Stovec's own investment plans. The only rupee capex figure disclosed is the capital-commitments note.

risks.risk: Technological disruption and obsolescence in printing
risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns: the pace of innovation in digital printing, automation and AI-enabled workflows continues to accelerate; companies may struggle to keep up with investments in the latest equipment and software, risking obsolescence or loss of competitive advantage. For a maker of rotary screens and rotary machines, a faster-than-expected shift to digital printing is a direct threat to the installed base.

risks.risk: Demand volatility and customer capex cycles, especially in Asia-Pacific
risks.note: MD&A Challenges: Asia-Pacific faces demand fluctuations from global economic uncertainty, inflationary pressure and changing trade dynamics; variations in customer investment cycles and export-oriented manufacturing activity may impact order visibility and capital expenditure decisions. This bit in the year under review - weak demand led to lower sales and profitability, with operating profit margin down to 3.77% from 6.66%.

MD&A Risks and Concerns: fluctuating prices of raw materials (paper, inks, chemicals, textiles) and increases in energy and transportation costs can compress margins, especially when customers resist price increases. Regulatory cost shocks bite too - the year's margin decline was partly an additional provision for gratuity and leave encashment under the New Labour Code, 2025.

risks.risk: Supply chain vulnerability and input availability
risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns: global disruptions such as geopolitical tensions, port delays or shortages of critical components can affect production timelines and inventory availability, leading to service delays or higher costs. Compounded by the Company operating across multiple international markets from a single Indian manufacturing base.

MD&A Risks and Concerns: intense price competition from regional players and low-cost providers can erode long-term contracts and profitability; MD&A Challenges separately flags pricing pressure from regional and low-cost players particularly in Asia-Pacific.

risks.risk: Concentration: single business activity, single manufacturing location, and dependence on the parent group
risks.note: Structural concentrations disclosed in BRSR and the accounts rather than labelled as risks - 100% of turnover from one manufacturing activity (rotary/digital printing machines, engravers, nickel screens and consumables), with 83.30% from Textile Consumables and Graphics Products; all plants and offices at one Ahmedabad premises with no international sites; exports 27.44% of turnover; SPGPrints B.V. holds 71.06% and the Company transacts across SPGPrints Group companies as related-party business, so its role, pricing and market access depend on Group decisions such as the restructuring that made it lead entity for the Textile Business.

risks.risk: Changing customer expectations and talent/skill gaps in advanced systems
risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns: customers now expect faster turnaround, highly customized products and integrated digital-to-physical solutions, and failure to meet these can cause client attrition; separately, advanced digital and hybrid systems require skilled operators and technicians, and a shortage of trained personnel or slow upskilling can impact productivity and quality.

risks.risk: Sustainability, regulatory compliance and cybersecurity exposure
risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns: increasing focus on environmental impact and regulatory compliance (waste management, emissions, chemical restrictions) requires ongoing investment, and failing to meet evolving sustainability standards may harm reputation and market access; as workflows become more digitized and connected, cybersecurity threats pose operational and reputational risks. The Board's Report states no material cyber security incidents, data breaches or loss of information were reported during the year, and that the Audit Committee oversees the risk management system.
